item.title: ICE Arrests Surge at Airports, Opening New Front in Deportation Drive
item.description: Federal agents are arresting spouses of Americans, tech workers and others whose visas have expired, including many who have active applications to stay in the country.

item.title: A U.S. Citizen Deleted His Phone’s Data. Now He Faces a Felony Charge.
item.description: Federal prosecutors charged a man returning to the United States with obstruction because he gave them a passcode that erased his smartphone during a customs search.
item.dc:creator: Adeel Hassan
item.media:description: A U.S. citizen used an open-source operating system, GrapheneOS, on his Google Pixel phone to “delete the digital contents,” before the device was seized, an indictment against the man said.

item.title: Gunther von Hagens, Creator of Polarizing ‘Body Worlds’ Exhibits, Dies at 81
item.description: A German scientist, he developed a process for turning corpses into posable figures. His shows drew millions of visitors, and many detractors.

item.media:description: Gunther von Hagens in 2002 with a flayed, bisected human specimen used in one of his “Body Worlds” exhibitions. In the late 1970s, he developed plastination, the method of making corpses into malleable figures.
